caeb0fa00d280e36662213b0a04f2d5e632553d3: Steibis (Oberstaufen) is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 18 km of runs offering an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts at all. Steibis (Oberstaufen)'s family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. Steibis (Oberstaufen)'s moderate altitude — starting at 859 m, topping out at 1338 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly recommended. The budget for a stay in Steibis (Oberstaufen) is clearly high: a day lift pass at 52€, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of quality — but be aware of it before you set off. In short: Steibis (Oberstaufen) doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.

caf1bb9918afb2c64194c898d415f139f57fc14a: The Val Thorens ski area, with its 150 km of runs, offers a strong choice for every type of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. If you want to enjoy the mountain by day as much as the evenings, Val Thorens is clearly one of the best options in its massif. As for snow reliability, Val Thorens is in a strong position with its highest point at 3230 m: even in capricious winters, the upper runs hold well until April. Budget-wise, a stay in Val Thorens is clearly high: the day lift pass costs 74€, on top of accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps.
